chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah and ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Īsā, from Samā‘ah, who said:
I asked him about the wounds of women, and he said: “Men and women are equal in the diyah until it reaches one-third; then when it exceeds one-third, it becomes like half of the diyah of a man.”

key_terms.الثُّلُثَ: one-third, the threshold mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial blood-compensation due for injury or killing
key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women, in the context of injury compensation
key_terms.دِيَةِ الرَّجُلِ: the diyah assigned to a man, used here as the legal measure
key_terms.نِصْفِ: half, indicating the reduced compensation beyond the threshold

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyah for women's injuries in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding diyah for injuries suffered by women. It states that men and women are equal in diyah up to one-third, and when the amount exceeds one-third, the compensation for a woman is calculated as half of the diyah of a man.
